## What this is

This article explains a way to use EJAM in R even if you do not have access to R on your own
computer. Codespaces provide a way to use EJAM functions in R when a) you do not want to install R,
or b) you temporarily only have access to a web browser. Using EJAM in R is useful in a few
scenarios:

1.  [Running EJAM functions in RStudio](analyzing.html) gives you access to analysis features not
    available in the web app, such as
    [`ejamit_compare_distances()`](https://public-environmental-data-partners.github.io/EJAM/reference/ejamit_compare_distances.html).
2.  Running your own private copy of the EJAM web app using `ejamapp(isPublic = FALSE)` lets you
    access the advanced tab and more options than are in the public hosted app.
3.  It also lets you test an app feature you have drafted but not yet deployed.

A GitHub codespace is a private Linux computer in the cloud that you use through a web browser. The
EJAM repository has a setup folder, `.devcontainer`, that makes a new codespace arrive with R,
RStudio and the EJAM package already installed. For how codespaces work in general, see
[GitHub's documentation on Codespaces](https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces).

## Caveats

-   **This is experimental and unsupported.** It has had only limited testing, nothing checks it
    automatically, and it may stop working when R, RStudio or EJAM's dependencies change. It is not
    a replacement for the public web app or for installing the package (see
    [Installing the EJAM R package](installing.html)).
-   **Some things do not work in a codespace.** Some functions that open a file or folder for you,
    such as plain `ejam2report(out)`, make the file but cannot display it. See "Limits".
-   **Your browser may silently block the new tabs.** RStudio and the EJAM web app each open in a
    new browser tab. A pop-up blocker can stop that with no message at all, or with a question
    that is hidden behind another window, so it looks as if nothing happened. See Step 2 for what
    to do.
-   **The first start is slow.** Setup takes about 15 minutes, and the page shows only "Setting up
    remote connection" during that time. Later starts of the same codespace take about a minute.
-   **You choose how much memory the machine has, and it must be enough for your analysis.** The
    2-core machine (8 GB) is enough to try EJAM on a small number of sites. Choose the 4-core
    machine (16 GB) or larger to analyze thousands of sites. With too little memory, R stops in the
    middle of an analysis.
-   **A codespace stops by itself when it is not being used.** See "If the codespace stops".

## What you need

-   A free GitHub account. You do not need to be a member of the project.
-   A web browser. A laptop or desktop is easiest. A tablet works, with the differences noted below.

Light use normally costs nothing. GitHub normally counts the time against the account of the person
who creates the codespace, and gives each personal account a free monthly allowance. See "What it
costs" below, including the case where an organization pays instead.

## Which version of EJAM you get

A codespace installs EJAM from the branch it was created from. You choose the branch when you create
the codespace, and nothing in the setup changes it afterwards.

-   The link in Step 1 creates the codespace from the `development` branch, so you get the
    development version. This is the intended use.
-   The setup works only on a branch that contains the `.devcontainer` folder. For now that is
    `development`. The repository's default branch, `main`, holds the latest release and does not
    have the folder yet, so a codespace made with the green **Code** button on the repository's main
    page is a plain one, with no R, RStudio or EJAM.
-   On the page where you confirm the new codespace, the **Branch** box shows which branch will be
    used, and you can change it there.

The large datasets are the data release that the chosen branch asks for.

## Step 1: Start a codespace

1.  Sign in to GitHub.
2.  Open this link:
    <span style="font-size: 1.2em;">**[create a codespace on the development branch of EJAM](https://codespaces.new/Public-Environmental-Data-Partners/EJAM/tree/development)**</span>.
3.  Check that Branch says `development`.
4.  Leave Machine type on 2-core to try things out. Choose 4-core (16 GB of memory) to
    analyze thousands of sites.
5.  Click **Create codespace**.
6.  Wait, and leave the tab open. The page says "Setting up remote connection" for the whole setup,
    about 15 minutes, because EJAM is installed and about 1 GB of data is downloaded before anything
    else appears. Then an editor called VS Code opens in the tab.
7.  If a grey bar at the top says Restricted Mode, click Manage and then Trust. RStudio
    does not start until you do. The folder is the EJAM repository itself.

## Step 2: Open RStudio

1.  In the bottom panel of VS Code, click the **Ports** tab (next to **Terminal**).
2.  Find the row named **RStudio (8787)**. If the row shows only the number 8787, RStudio is still
    starting, so wait until its name appears.
3.  **Click the globe icon** in that row, just right of the web address. RStudio opens in a new
    browser tab with no password to enter.

**The first try often fails.** If the new tab stays on "getting your codespace ready", or shows a
`localhost` address and an error saying the browser could not connect to the server, close that tab
and click the globe icon again. The second try usually works.

**Your browser may block a new tab without telling you.** RStudio and the EJAM web app each open in
a new tab, and a browser's pop-up blocker can stop a new tab silently: nothing appears, and there is
no message. Tablets and phones do this most often. The browser may instead ask whether to allow the
pop-up, but that question can be hidden behind another window or panel, so look for it. *If the
browser does ask whether to allow a pop-up, allow it.* How to stop the blocking depends on your
browser and device, so look in its settings or help pages for pop-ups. For example, in Safari on an
iPad, tap the page menu button at the left end of the address bar and choose **Turn Off Content
Blockers**.

Leave the port set to **Private**. *Do not click Make Public*: RStudio here has no password, so a
public port would let anyone with the link run code in your codespace.

You can ignore the other rows in the Ports list, and any `[rserver] WARNING` lines in the terminal.

## Step 3: Try EJAM functions

When RStudio opens, it runs `library(EJAM)` for you. That loads EJAM's block data and builds a
search index, which takes a minute or two. Wait until the messages stop and the console shows the
`>` prompt. The same happens each time R restarts.

Then, in the RStudio console:

```{r}
out <- ejamit(testpoints_10, radius = 1)
ejam2report(out, filename = path.expand("~/ejam_report.html"), launch_browser = FALSE)
browseURL(path.expand("~/ejam_report.html"))
```

The first line analyzes ten example sites. The second saves a summary report in your home folder,
and the third opens it in a new browser tab. Each time R opens a new tab, the browser may ask again
whether to allow the pop-up (see Step 2).

Plain `ejam2report(out)` makes the report but cannot display it in a codespace, and the "To open
that folder from R" hint that it prints does not work there either.

These also work in a codespace:

```{r}
ejam2barplot(out)   # bar plot, shown in the Plots pane
ejam2map(out)       # interactive map, opened in a new browser tab
ejam2excel(out, save_now = TRUE, fname = path.expand("~/ejam_results.xlsx"))
ejam2report(out, fileextension = "pdf", filename = path.expand("~/ejam_report.pdf"),
            launch_browser = FALSE)   # the report as a PDF file
```

The spreadsheet is saved in your home folder. If the console shows an "Error converting HTML to PNG"
message, the spreadsheet is still saved, but without the picture of the report (see "Limits").

### Finding the files you saved

The examples above save files in your home folder, `/home/rstudio`. RStudio's **Files** pane starts
in a different folder, `/workspaces/EJAM`, which holds the EJAM source code, so the saved files are
not in view at first. To show the home folder in the **Files** pane, run:

```{r}
rstudioapi::filesPaneNavigate("~")
```

Then click the **Files** tab, because RStudio may still be showing the **Plots** or **Viewer** tab.

Or click the **...** button at the right end of the path shown at the top of the **Files** pane and
enter `~`.

If a file you just saved is not listed, click the refresh icon at the top right of the **Files**
pane.

Once you can see a file there:

-   Click an `.html` file and choose **View in Web Browser** to open it in a new tab.
-   To download any file to your own computer, tick its box and choose **More \> Export**.

### Using your own sites

Use the **Upload** button in the **Files** pane to add a spreadsheet of latitudes and longitudes,
then give its name to `ejamit()`. Files left in a codespace are lost when the codespace is deleted,
so download the results you want to keep.

### More to try

For a first tour, see [Basics - Quick Start Guide](basics.html). For the analysis features that are
available only from R and not in the web app, see
[Running EJAM functions in RStudio](analyzing.html).

## Step 4: Run the EJAM web app

In the RStudio console:

```{r}
ejamapp(isPublic = FALSE)
```

The app opens in a new window or tab, with more ways to choose sites than the public hosted app
offers. The **Advanced Settings** tab is not shown at first. To show it, use the option for it on
the **About** tab.

**If no new tab appears, the browser's pop-up blocker has probably stopped
it without telling you** (see Step 2). Allow pop-ups, then run the same line again.

This copy of the app is private to you and runs only while your codespace is
running. Click the red stop button in the RStudio console to end it.

In the app, the report shown on screen, the HTML report download and the Excel download have been
tested and work. Downloading a report as a PDF from the app has not been tried in a codespace.

## If the codespace stops

A codespace shuts itself down after a period without activity. This is normal. The period is 30
minutes unless you have changed it in your GitHub settings (**Settings \> Codespaces \> Default
idle timeout**, from 5 to 240 minutes). Work done only in the RStudio tab may not count as activity,
so a codespace can stop while RStudio is open.

When it stops, the RStudio tab stops responding or shows an error. Files you saved are kept, and
EJAM stays installed, but the R session is interrupted: anything that was running is cut off, the
app is no longer running, and objects such as `out` may be gone. To continue:

1.  Go to [your codespaces list](https://github.com/codespaces), click **...** next to the
    codespace, then **Open in Browser**. It starts in about a minute.
2.  Open RStudio again as in Step 2.
3.  Wait for EJAM to load again, then repeat your analysis.

## When you are done

-   **Stop it.** Click the blue **Codespaces** box at the bottom-left corner of the VS Code tab and
    choose **Stop Current Codespace**. A stopped codespace uses none of your time allowance.
-   **Come back later.** Go to [your codespaces list](https://github.com/codespaces), click **...**
    next to the codespace, then **Open in Browser**. It starts in about a minute and EJAM is still
    installed. Repeat Step 2 to open RStudio.
-   **Delete it.** In the same **...** menu, choose **Delete** when you no longer need it, because a
    stored codespace counts against your storage allowance. By default GitHub deletes a codespace by
    itself after 30 days without use. The period can be shorter, because you can change it in your
    GitHub settings (**Settings \> Codespaces \> Default retention period**) and an organization
    can limit it, so check that setting and do not rely on files staying there.

A codespace keeps the version of EJAM it installed when it was created. To get newer development
code, delete it and create a new one.

## What it costs

GitHub normally counts usage against the personal account of the person who creates the codespace.
The exception is an organization that has chosen to pay for codespaces its members or collaborators
create from its repositories. Then the organization is billed, and the personal allowance and
spending limit described here do not apply; see
[GitHub's page on who owns and pays for codespaces](https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces/managing-codespaces-for-your-organization/choosing-who-owns-and-pays-for-codespaces-in-your-organization).
The page where you confirm a new codespace says who will be billed.

For a codespace billed to your personal account, these figures are from late 2026; check
[GitHub's Codespaces billing page](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-codespaces)
for current ones. A free personal account includes 120 core-hours and 15 GB-months of storage each
month.

| Machine | Memory | Running time the free allowance covers | Price beyond the allowance |
|---------|--------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| 2-core  | 8 GB   | 60 hours a month                       | \$0.18 an hour             |
| 4-core  | 16 GB  | 30 hours a month                       | \$0.36 an hour             |

Storage is the part to watch. This codespace fills most of its 32 GB disk, so keeping one for about
two weeks uses the month's free storage. For personal accounts, by default GitHub blocks further use
when the free allowance runs out and does not charge you, unless you have added a payment method and set a
spending limit above zero.

## Limits

| What you see | What to do |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| R stops, or RStudio says the session crashed during an analysis | The machine ran out of memory. In [your codespaces list](https://github.com/codespaces), choose **... \> Change machine type**, pick 4-core, then stop and reopen the codespace. Nothing is reinstalled. |
| A "Low disk space" warning | Expected. The disk is nearly full after setup. Download the results you want and avoid storing large files. |
| The RStudio console says there is no package called EJAM | Setup did not finish. In the VS Code **Terminal**, run `bash .devcontainer/setup.sh` and wait for `EJAM ... is ready.` |
| RStudio or the app does not open, and there is no error message | The browser's pop-up blocker stopped the new tab. Allow pop-ups in your browser, then click the globe icon again (Step 2) or run `ejamapp(isPublic = FALSE)` again. |
| No **RStudio (8787)** row in **Ports** | In the VS Code **Terminal**, run `rserver`, then look at **Ports** again. |
| A function asks for a Census API key | Functions that download American Community Survey data need a free key. Set it with `Sys.setenv(CENSUS_API_KEY = "your key")`. |
| A PDF report fails with "Cannot find headless Chrome" | The setup adds a setting that PDF reports need, and it is missing. In the VS Code **Terminal**, run `bash .devcontainer/setup.sh`, then in RStudio choose **Session \> Restart R**. Or use the HTML report or the Excel file. |
| `ejam2excel()` prints "Error converting HTML to PNG" | The spreadsheet is still saved, without the picture of the report. Making that picture does not always work in a codespace. Run the line again, or use the Excel download in the app. |
| No R code completion in VS Code | It is switched off to leave enough memory for EJAM. RStudio has its own code completion. |

On a tablet, VS Code's keyboard shortcuts are missing, so use the menu button at the top left of
the VS Code tab. The report shown inside the app works on a tablet, interactive map included. A
report file downloaded to a tablet and reopened there may lose the map, because some tablets show
saved HTML files in a simplified preview. The Excel download opens normally, with a static picture
of the report and map.

## How it is set up

Two files in the `.devcontainer` folder of the repository define the codespace:

-   `devcontainer.json` names the base image (R with the system libraries that mapping packages
    need), adds RStudio Server, and says what to run at startup.
-   `setup.sh` installs EJAM from the checked-out branch, downloads its large datasets, clears the
    download cache, and adds a few lines to an R startup file so that RStudio runs `library(EJAM)`
    when it starts and so that PDF reports can start the Chromium browser.

Codespaces that are built ahead of time ("prebuilds") are not turned on, so every new codespace runs
the whole setup.
